doc.title: Billie Pierce and De De Pierce Interview, 1959-10-07

title: The St. Bernard trio and who went to Bunkie
summary: Billie lists the three-piece group, then the musicians she took to Bunkie, including Kid Ernest and Frank Gibbs.

story.theme_name: Remembering the early trumpeters and their styles
story.community_name: Buddy Bolden and Buddy Petit: the trumpet legends

blocks.x: Who was with you at this place at St. Bernard and St. Claude?
Let me see. Who had one drum? Was it Albert Jive? Albert. Right. I had Albert Jive on drums, D on trumpet, I'm on piano, just three pieces.
And from there you went to Bunky?
From there I went to Bunky. Yeah.
And who did you take the Bunky?

Uh, Paul Mouye and his brother Ernest. Ernest, he's. Ernest, he's. Ernest, he's. He's past, he's past. He's past, you know. He's past, he's past. Kid Ernest. Kid Ernest. Kid Ernest. I take him out the Bunky with me. Oh, he's quick to look at my kid. Well, they didn't have no wives, you see, and they couldn't make the trip. The other boys married, they couldn't leave the family, see. The only way I did with me.

I didn't wait for Stale. The other business got low. It's kind of low, so he decided. Decided. Yeah, then he went to Texas and we'll be playing when we came back home. Yeah. Yeah, I played in Texas. I mean, he still wanted us to go out there. Yeah, I didn't want to play. There you go.
Did you have a trombone in Bunky?
Yeah, Frank Gibbs. Give up. Oh, he's a wonderful trombone. Wonderful man. Yeah, Frank Gibbs.
He's a cripple too, you know. He's a, I mean, it's kind of cool.
